What Are TMJ Disorders?

The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is the hinge that connects your jawbone to your skull, allowing you to chew, speak, and yawn. When this joint becomes strained, injured, or misaligned, it can lead to temporomandibular disorders (TMD). These conditions often cause ongoing discomfort that affects more than just your jaw.
Common causes of TMJ disorders include:

children.title: Arthritis or inflammation in the joint
Injury to the jaw or face

children.html: Typical symptoms may include:

children.title: Clicking, popping, or locking of the jaw
Difficulty chewing or opening your mouth fully
Neck or shoulder pain from muscle tension

children.html: Who Is a Candidate for TMJ Treatment?

Have you been searching for TMJ treatment near me? Not every case of jaw tension requires professional care, but if your symptoms are frequent or getting worse, it may be time to see a TMJ specialist in Valencia. Seeking treatment early can prevent long-term complications and protect your teeth and jaw health.
Signs You Need TMJ Treatment:

items.text: Frequent Jaw Pain or Stiffness: Discomfort that often appears in the morning or after chewing can signal strain on the joint.
Clicking, Popping, or Locking of the Jaw: Sounds or limited movement during everyday functions like eating or speaking may point to TMJ issues.
Recurring Headaches or Earaches: Tension in the jaw muscles can radiate, creating pain in the head, ears, and even the temples.
Difficulty Chewing: Pain or restricted movement when biting or chewing harder foods is a common indicator.
Nighttime Teeth Grinding or Clenching: This habit, often noticed by a partner, can wear down teeth and worsen jaw tension.
Neck or Shoulder Pain: Muscle strain from TMJ dysfunction sometimes spreads beyond the jaw to surrounding areas.
